recommendations.why: How consistently a set of rating items measures one thing, before you add them up into a score, with a check of how each item fits the rest. It uses revenue (f64), seats (u16) and score (f64).

alternatives.when: you only want to see which items go together, pair by pair
you want a p-value for one pair of items

recommendations.why: Adds to every row its score on a rating battery: the average of its answered items or a prorated total, reverse-worded items flipped. It uses revenue (f64), seats (u16) and score (f64).

alternatives.when: you want how consistently the items measure one thing
the items should be weighted by how much each reflects a common trait
you want an arbitrary formula of the items

recommendations.why: Checks whether a set of numeric fields are related at all, the first check before summarising them as a few underlying dimensions. It uses revenue (f64), seats (u16) and score (f64).

alternatives.when: you want how strongly each pair is related

recommendations.why: Which hidden qualities a set of related measures reflects, and how strongly each measure is tied to each, before building scale scores. It uses revenue (f64), seats (u16) and score (f64).

alternatives.when: you want summaries of all the spread, not just what the measures share
you already know the items measure one quality and want its reliability

follow_ups.when: the items of one factor are to be added up into a score

recommendations.why: How many underlying dimensions a set of related measures covers and which measures belong to each, so a few summaries can stand in for many. It uses revenue (f64), seats (u16) and score (f64).

alternatives.when: you want to check that one set of items measures a single quality reliably
you only want to see which measures go together, pair by pair

recommendations.why: Adds to every row its score on one factor behind several related numeric fields: an estimate of the hidden trait they measure together. It uses revenue (f64), seats (u16) and score (f64). Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

needs.why: Choose which factor to score, counting from 1 for the one that accounts for the most variance.

alternatives.when: you want how many factors there are and which fields load on each
you want a summary of all the fields' variance rather than a common trait

recommendations.why: Adds to every row its score on one principal component of several related numeric fields: one number standing in for what they share. It uses revenue (f64), seats (u16) and score (f64). Fill in each placeholder in the draft before you run it.

needs.why: Choose which component to score, counting from 1 for the largest.

alternatives.when: you want how many dimensions there are and which fields load on each
you want how unusual a row is across the fields
